articles.headline: NBA issues new guidelines, instructs refs to crack down on push-offs
articles.description: The NBA has issued new guidance to its referees on four types of "high-volume and highly impactful" calls, including push-offs.
articles.body:
The NBA has instructed its referees to crack down on offensive players who use their arms to push off against defensive players during the upcoming season, one of several new points of emphasis for officials, the league announced on a conference call Tuesday.

James Jones, the NBA's executive vice president of basketball operations, said the league has issued new guidance on four types of "high-volume and highly impactful" calls, including push-offs. The NBA's goal, James said, is to ensure that "the way our game is played, and the way our game presents, continues to track favorably" for players and fans.

A push-off most commonly occurs when an offensive player uses his non-dribbling arm to contact a defensive player so that he can create space to attempt a shot from the perimeter. While some level of jockeying between offensive players and defensive players is legal and to be expected, the NBA's referees will now use the "Four F's" framework to determine if they should call an offensive foul on a push off:

The "Four F's" are feeling, firming, force and full extension.

Referees have been instructed that a ball handler is allowed to use his off arm to "feel" his opponent or to "firm up" by gathering himself in front of a defensive player. However, referees should assess an offensive foul if the ball handler's off arm contacts the defender with "force" or is "fully extended" to create an advantage.

"We've got to make sure the defensive side of the ball does not get penalized by allowing illegal acts by the offensive player," said Monty McCutchen, the NBA's senior vice president of referee development and training. "I think we can do a better job."

The new guidance on push-offs comes during the middle of an ongoing scoring boom: NBA teams averaged 115.6 points last season, the highest mark since the 1969-70 season. In recent years, the NBA has sought to cut down on other illegal actions by offensive players, such as stopping short to create collisions, splaying legs during shot attempts and jumping sideways into defenders to draw free throws.

Michael Jordan authored perhaps the most famous push-off in NBA history when he freed himself from Utah Jazz guard Bryon Russell for a midrange jumper in the closing seconds of Game 6 of the 1998 NBA Finals. No offensive foul was called, Jordan made the shot and the Bulls won their sixth championship of the 1990s.

By the NBA's new "Four F's" standard, Jordan wouldn't be whistled for an offensive foul against Russell because he didn't contact Russell's body with noticeable "force" or fully extend his left arm.

The NBA released a video Tuesday featuring several push-offs that it would deem to be offensive fouls under its new framework. In one clip, then-Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown raised his right forearm and shoved into the chest of then-Philadelphia 76ers forward Kelly Oubre Jr. to set up a jumper near the free throw line.

articles.headline: Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil averaged record 24.9M viewers
articles.description: The Ravens' 34-31 victory over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, averaged 24.9 million viewers on CBS on Sunday, making it the most-watched NFL international game in history.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Ravens' 34-31 victory over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, averaged 24.9 million viewers on CBS on Sunday, making it the most-watched NFL international game in history.

According to Nielsen, the audience peaked to more than 30 million during the late stages when Baltimore's Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal on the last play. It also was the most-watched Week 3 game on CBS since 2014.

This year's Week 1 game in Australia between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams averaged 18.5 million in the U.S. on Netflix. Last year's Week 1 Friday night game in Brazil between the Los Angeles Chargers and Kansas City Chiefs also averaged 18.5 million on YouTube.

Sunday's CBS doubleheader averaged 21.45 million, its most-watched September doubleheader since 2014.

The other six international games last year were on NFL Network and averaged 6.2 million.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Kessler talks up Lakers' title hopes behind 'nasty' defense
articles.description: New addition Walker Kessler is convinced the Lakers have the right guys to be "a nasty defensive team" and a contender in the Western Conference this season.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The Los Angeles Lakers' offense has thrived since Luka Doncic arrived in 2025, but center Walker Kessler needed only one day of training camp to be convinced the team's defense will hold up its end of the bargain this season.

"Listen, I think we're going to be a nasty defensive team," Kessler said Tuesday. "I think people aren't taking into account how good our perimeter defense is going to be. A lot of guys are very smart on the perimeter and positionally can play really good defense. We have guys who are just ball hawks."

During JJ Redick's two seasons as coach, the Lakers have ranked above average in offensive efficiency and below average in defensive efficiency. After a transformative summer that saw the departure of LeBron James and several other veteran players, the Lakers are hoping to establish a more aggressive defensive identity with a rebuilt roster that includes Doncic, guard Austin Reaves, Kessler and a deep group of young wings.

Redick said Tuesday that his first goal during training camp was to "establish our defensive principles." With both forward spots in the starting lineup open for competition, Redick said he met with the team's wings last week to give them their marching orders.

"They understood the assignment today," he said. "That was exciting. They set the tone for us defensively. There was a lot of physicality, a lot of grabbing and holding, and a lot of disruption without gambling."

The 7-foot-2 Kessler, who was traded by the Utah Jazz to the Lakers this summer, will serve as the back-line rim protector after averaging 2.4 blocks per game during his first four seasons.

"The paint is kind of closed when [Kessler] is on the court," Doncic said.

From there, Doncic's remade supporting cast includes defensive specialists Jarred Vanderbilt and Matisse Thybulle as well as free agent additions Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams. Kevon Looney, a veteran center who won two championships with the Golden State Warriors, will back up Kessler.

Kessler praised Looney for his "mind and positioning," Vanderbilt for his skill defending all five positions, and Thybulle, Grimes, Sexton and Williams for their ability to apply defensive pressure.

"Having those guys that can steal the ball ... [and] when they do get beat, be able to recover, it makes my job a lot easier," he said. "It's a lot easier to block a shot when a dude has someone on his hip instead of an open lane towards the basket."

The Lakers boasted the NBA's No. 3 defense when they won the 2020 championship and the No. 1 defense during the 2020-21 regular season. But their performance on that end has slipped noticeably in the years that followed.

articles.headline: Guard Sam Cosmi, safety Nick Cross out for London game vs. Colts
articles.description: Commanders guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross did not travel with the team to London on Tuesday night for their Week 4 game against the Colts.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders ruled out two starters for Sunday's game in London, though three others remain a possibility to return. Guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross did not travel with the team to London on Tuesday night for their Week 4 game against the Colts.

Both were considered long shots to make the trip; each was hurt in Week 2 at Dallas. Cosmi suffered a concussion late in the 37-20 loss while Cross played despite an injury the team has described as "internal" but needed to have surgery after the game and stayed overnight at a hospital in Dallas.

Three other injured starters did accompany Washington (1-2) to London, as coach Dan Quinn said they would on Monday: quarterback Jayden Daniels (elbow), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin). Quinn said all three would participate in at least some portion of practice this week. Washington will have a light workout Wednesday after arriving earlier that morning.

Daniels sustained his injury in Week 2 but is considered week-to-week. Because it's to his left and non-throwing elbow, he has already resumed some throwing. Marcus Mariota would start against the Colts if Daniels can't play.

If Luvu can't play, then Kain Medrano would start alongside rookie Sonny Styles. Both players intercepted a pass in Sunday's 33-31 win over Seattle. Medrano, a 2025 fifth-round pick, returned his 50 yards for a touchdown. He opened the season as the Commanders' fifth inside linebacker and a special teams performer, but injuries forced him into his first snaps from scrimmage in the NFL. Leo Chenal fractured his neck in that win and Jordan Magee injured his hamstring in Week 1 and is on injured reserve.

Okonkwo, like Luvu, has missed the last two weeks.

With Cosmi once again sidelined, Nick Allegretti is expected to start at right guard with veteran Lucas Patrick at center. Patrick, signed after Week 1, left Sunday's win with a boot on his left foot. He missed four snaps during the game because of an ankle injury.

articles.headline: Cowboys' Schottenheimer 'aligned' with Jones after Rio gaffes
articles.description: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he would "be better" after meeting with Jerry Jones about questionable late-game coaching decisions in Sunday's loss to the Ravens.
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones did not mask disappointment with the decisions made in the final 28 seconds of Sunday's loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

Jones and coach Brian Schottenheimer went through the end-of-game decisions, from the playcalling after the Cowboys faced first-and-goal from the 2, to Dak Prescott's third-down throwaway that led to a tying field goal, to how the subsequent kickoff and seven seconds were handled, allowing the Ravens to kick a winning field goal with a second to play.

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday morning. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. [The coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with. ... But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again. You can't get that back. [There's] no way to get it back. What you can do is use it ... to get better. That's what's being done."

Schottenheimer accepted responsibility with Jones and publicly in his first comments after the team's return from Brazil.

"I'm man enough to take mistakes. I make a lot of mistakes. I'm certainly not perfect," Schottenheimer said. "And I know one thing, Jerry and I had a very good conversation about it. I explained it. He understands. He understands that there was a mistake that was made, and he was terrific. Great, sound advice. I value him. He's been around the game a long time, just like I have, and he's seen a lot of stuff.

"And so to me, that shows that he and I are aligned very closely. This will make me better. I'll be better. And again, I'm looking forward to lining up and playing this week against the Texans."

Schottenheimer added, "I hurt our chance to win that game and I'll be better. And I'm better than that. I'm better than I performed in the last 28 seconds."

After the game, Schottenheimer said he "overcoached" Prescott on the third-down pass to George Pickens that was a throwaway.

"I trust Dak Prescott completely, so it was the word that I chose, which I'm not going to give away," Schottenheimer said. "The words that we say have meaning, and when I said the word, it put him into a mindset that he doesn't play with. He doesn't play that way. He doesn't play the game that way. And so that's what I would change."

After Brandon Aubrey tied the score with a 23-yard field goal, the Cowboys had him kick the ball through the end zone for a touchback. The Ravens took over at their own 35, and quarterback Lamar Jackson hit receiver Zay Flowers for a 27-yard completion to set up the 56-yard kick from Tyler Loop with one second left.

In retrospect, Aubrey's kickoff should have been short to burn time off the clock.

Schottenheimer said his emotions of the third-down call affected the kickoff decision, adding that the communication between special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen and game management coordinator Ryan Feder was not good enough either.

articles.headline: Sources: NBA reviewing bids from three finalists for Vegas team
articles.description: The NBA is expected to select the winning bid for owner of the Las Vegas expansion team from among three finalist groups: Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo.
articles.body:
The NBA is expected to select the winning bid for ownership of the Las Vegas expansion team in the very near future, with a price of at least $12 billion to $13 billion for the franchise and a new arena, from among three finalist groups -- Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo -- sources told ESPN.

The league, which will hold a formal approval process by the end of December on two expansion teams, is closing on Las Vegas before Seattle for several reasons. Las Vegas has a livelier bidding market with higher offers, and the process consists of the logistics of developing a new arena versus Climate Pledge Arena already being a ready-made home for the Seattle team. And the Las Vegas runners-up also could join the Seattle bid process.

The NBA has targeted as soon as the 2028-29 season for the expansion teams, sources said.

Nancy Walton Laurie is the daughter of Walmart co-founder James "Bud" Walton. Her husband, Bill Laurie, is a former owner of the NHL's St. Louis Blues. The two have a home in Henderson, Nevada, a suburb of Las Vegas, and they have a net worth of $17 billion, according to Forbes.

 

Apostolopoulos, a Canadian billionaire, discussed buying the Charlotte Hornets from Michael Jordan in 2023 but instead focused on purchasing the NFL's Washington Commanders. That franchise was later sold for $6.05 billion to a group led by Josh Harris, who also owns the Philadelphia 76ers and the NHL's New Jersey Devils. Apostolopoulos has a known desire to build a wide-ranging portfolio across multiple sports leagues.

Apostolopoulos and his brothers, Jim and Peter Apostolopoulos, lead the group, with Lasry as a partner.

Lasry is the former co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks. In 2023, he sold his stake to Cleveland Browns owners Jimmy and Dee Haslam at a valuation of $3.5 billion. Lasry bought the Bucks for $550 million in 2014 from former U.S. Senator Herb Kohl and was the team's governor when Milwaukee won the NBA title in 2021.

Lasry is currently the chairman and CEO of Avenue Capital, which last year closed its Avenue Sports Fund with over $1 billion in commitments. The fund invests in teams, leagues and sports-related businesses.

Colangelo, the former owner of the Phoenix Suns, said in July he was entering the bidding with his Las Vegas Jacks group. His announcement came one month after Foley, the majority owner of the NHL's Vegas Golden Knights, said he wanted to bring an NBA team to the city.

Colangelo's group and Foley began talking about joining forces four months ago, and they have agreed to partner because of Foley's ties to the city combined with the Jacks' plans for a new arena and the group's relationship equity with key league stakeholders. Foley said in June that his potential NBA franchise would play at T-Mobile Arena, where his Golden Knights have games, but sources said a new arena will be built if the Colangelo-Foley group wins the bid.

articles.headline: Steelers' Ramsey says he has broken wrist, uncertain for Thursday
articles.description: Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey said he would "try" to play Thursday night against the Browns despite saying he broke his wrist in the team's Week 3 win.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey said he broke his right wrist early in last Sunday's win against the Cincinnati Bengals, but despite the fracture, Ramsey said "of course" he's going to "try to" play against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night.

"I got to be able to protect it, obviously," Ramsey said Tuesday. "[It's a] broken wrist, so it's not like I can't really do anything about it. It's just going to be about seeing if I'm able to protect it and also still be myself in a good enough capacity where I feel like if I go out there, I won't be letting any of my teammates down."

Ramsey, 31, said he sustained the injury on the first series of the Week 3 game. Even so, he still played every defensive snap and finished with eight tackles.

"It was hurting," Ramsey said of how his wrist felt during the game. He added Tuesday that it felt "OK."

Listed as a limited participant in each of the practice estimations this week, Ramsey wore a sling Monday and what appeared to be a cast or brace Tuesday.

Asked if he would be able to play Thursday, Ramsey declined to give a definitive answer.

"We'll see," he said. "That's all I can give you, I think."

Ramsey's undetermined status is just one part of a Steelers' secondary that's in flux. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was estimated to be a full participant in each of the Steelers' walkthroughs this week, marking the first time that has happened since being activated off the physically unable to perform list in late August. Porter was dealing with a back injury amid contentious contract negotiations. The two sides didn't reach an agreement on an extension before the regular-season deadline, and Porter has been inactive for each of the first three weeks as he continues to ramp up in his conditioning.

Slot cornerback Brandin Echols is also uncertain for Thursday's game after entering concussion protocol against the Bengals. He was a limited participant in each of the Steelers' walkthroughs.

With the injuries and unpredictability in the secondary, the Steelers could turn to practice squad defensive back Doneiko Slaughter, who has been elevated in each of the first three games, to help in the slot. And it could also mean more playing time for rookie Daylen Everette, who initially came in against the Bengals when starting cornerback Jamel Dean left in the first half because of injury. Everette played nearly half of the defensive snaps and had a key pass breakup on third down. Dean returned in the second half, but Everette ended up playing alongside him and replaced Asante Samuel Jr.

"I was very impressed at how he responded because I remember being out as a rookie, you get the little jitters," Dean said of Everette being thrust into action. "But once he made his play, he kind of settled in. So I was like, OK, I see you. I love it."

articles.headline: Patriots place offensive lineman Greg Van Roten (thigh) on IR
articles.description: The Patriots placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday as the infrastructure around quarterback Drake Maye took another hit.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Infrastructure around struggling quarterback Drake Maye took another hit Tuesday when the New England Patriots placed veteran guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve -- another reminder that the team's run of good health contributing to its surprising run to Super Bowl LX hasn't carried into 2026.

Van Roten, who started in Sunday's blowout loss to the Jaguars in place of opening-day starter Mike Onwenu (broken ankle), is the 17th player the Patriots have placed on injured reserve and/or reached an injury settlement with this season. Last season, New England placed 16 players on injured reserve all season.

Among the 17 players the team has placed on injured reserve are Onwenu, No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown, No. 2 tight end Julian Hill, top backup safety Dell Pettus, top backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and punter Bryce Baringer.

Van Roten, 36, was knocked out of Sunday's game in the second quarter with a thigh injury, according to the team.

Maye, who threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in the game, faced a 47% pressure rate, according to ESPN Research. That is the highest rate he has faced this season and the fourth highest of his three-year career.

Maye went 4-of-9 with an interception when pressured Sunday and has completed 41% of his passes under pressure this season, with no touchdowns and three interceptions, according to ESPN Research.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel foreshadowed Monday that the team was preparing to be without Van Roten when he said backup center Ben Brown would likely take repetitions at right guard this week. When Van Roten left Sunday's game, third-year veteran Walter Rouse -- who was acquired from the Minnesota Vikings on Aug. 30 -- took his place.

New England had signed Van Roten, who is in his 12th NFL season, to a one-year, $3 million contract Aug.18.

The Patriots (1-2) visit the AFC East rival Buffalo Bills (3-0) on Sunday.

articles.headline: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy: Man City verdict could lead to Premier League expulsion
articles.description: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said Manchester City could be thrown out of the Premier League after being found guilty of all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.
articles.body:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said Manchester City could be thrown out of the Premier League after being found guilty of all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.

The league has said City breached its financial rules on a huge scale between 2009-10 and 2017-18 after arranging 'sham' commercial deals as part of a disguised funding scheme.

Nandy told Channel 5 News: "I don't want to preempt any kind of appeal process, and they are entitled to a fair hearing. But what I would say is that the ultimate sanction is very serious indeed.

"I mean, a club can be expelled from the Premier League if these sorts of allegations are upheld, with obviously huge repercussions for everybody.

"So there are very serious sanctions, and I think the bigger issue is how do we make sure that we have clearly understood rules that are upheld and applied consistently, and that we can move quickly when they're breached.

"The Premier League is one of our greatest exports. It brings joy to millions of people, and we want to make sure that we protect it for the fans for the future."

Former City chairman David Bernstein said the league's findings were "damning beyond belief" and that "the sanctions cannot just be financial".

Bernstein, who spent five years in the role before stepping down in 2003, also suggested the club's board should "be suspended immediately."

He told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It is damning beyond belief. My immediate thoughts are, should the board continue? Should the people involved be suspended immediately?

"Very, very serious. I think it's really terrible. There's a school of thought with lawyers that is 'deny, deny, deny', but this is a football club that is part of a league and the whole credibility of the league is at stake here.

"I would go as far [as to say it is a deep-seated form of fraud] and if it is, I'm not a lawyer but as a thought this is something so serious that it goes beyond the football authorities.

"The sanctions cannot just be financial, so it's got to be way beyond that. If the appeal fails, Manchester City cannot stay in the league, they have to suffer. And I say that as a supporter and a fan."

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire says City's breaches have "gone far beyond the worst-case scenario that anybody initially envisaged."

Maguire told BBC Radio 5 Live: "If you Google what the word 'sham' means, I'm getting the words 'fake, false, fraud'. It's very, very significant.

"I think the quantity of money involved -- [approximately] £900 million over a nine-year period -- is a staggering misstatement, and it looks like it's been a corroborative fraud.
